cvEn:
Simon Albert, son of Irma and Arthur, was born in 1904 in Königsberg, Germany. His father, Arthur, died on 17 April 1934. His sister Ruth married and emigrated to Eretz Israel in 1933 with her husband and son. In 1938 she managed to escape the Nazis: she left Danzig and emigrated with her husband and two daughters to Canada. That same year, Albert immigrated to Eretz Israel with his partner, Else, and the two settled in Haifa.

During the Second World War, Albert enlisted in the British Army and was posted to the Royal Army Service Corps. In December 1940 he was sent to Greece with the units that had come to assist the Greeks against the Italian invasion and then the German one. In June 1941 the British expeditionary forces surrendered to the Nazis on Crete. Albert fell on 2 Iyar 5701 (29 April 1941), and his place of burial is unknown. He left behind a mother, two sisters, a nephew, two nieces, and his partner. On 5 September 1942, his mother was murdered in the Holocaust in Riga, to which she had been deported from Berlin.

According to the research "The Prisoners of War Census," carried out in 2019 by the Forum of Families of Prisoners of War and Missing in Action, his British service number was PAL/866, with the 603 Pioneer Company, and his rank was Private. He is commemorated on the Athens Memorial in Athens, Greece, on Face 9.

Further details of his British Army service: Simon Albert (spelled Simon Albrt in the records), service number PAL/866, enlisted in the British Army in 1940. He was posted to the Royal Army Service Corps (R.A.S.C.), with the 232 Motor Transport unit. His military trade was driver. He was later transferred to the 603 Pioneer Company. His rank in the British Army was Private (Pte.). He was laid to rest in Athens Cemetery, Greece. Grave location: Face 9.
